newsitem.title: USA: G30 calls for measures to curb systemic risk.
newsitem.headline: G30 calls for measures to curb systemic risk.

text.p: The Group of Thirty called on global financial institutions and national supervisors to carry out a series of measures aimed at averting serious disruptions to the global financial system on Friday.

In a report titled "Global Institutions, National Supervision and Systemic Risk," the Group said that transnational banks must develop principles for risk management, external audit and reporting, which supervisors must then enforce.
The report also urged national legislatures to provide a sound legal basis for netting, enforceability of contracts and insolvency, expecially for cross-border transactions and activities.

The Group said that the global operations of financial institutions and markets have outgrown the national accounting, legal and supervisory systems on which the safety and soundness of individual institutions and the financial system rely.
Initiatives by national supervisors to enhance international cooperation in this area have been helpful, but more commitment from core financial institutions must follow, the study said.

The study recommended that these core institutions -- defined as large internationally active commercial banks and large investment banks -- establish a standing committee to develop global principles for risk management and submit their operations to an independent external global audit of perfomance and controls.
It advised supervisors to apply a framework based on the principles set out by these institutions and agree on consistent reporting requirements.
